BALFOUR CHOCOLATES AND CIGARETTES:

label: text
text: Eight additional cruisers and two destroyers were ordered by Mr. Baldwin's Government late in 1923 as a measure to relieve unemployment, but this total of cruisers was cut down by Mr. MacDonald's administration to five. Two cruisers, however, are to be built for the Australian Government, bringing the total laid down in 1924 to seven. The new vessels are intended to replace the cruisers of the County class, laid down twenty years or more ago. The lack of modern cruisers for service on distant stations has compelled the admiralty to employ light cruisers for that work at the cost of great discomfort to their crews.

label: text
text: A warm debate in the Chamber on the rioting in the Latin quarter on the 28th of last month terminated at three in the morning with a vote of confidence in the Government of 318 to 22. M. Albert, the Minister of Education, condemned the movement as political and refused to countenance sabotage in the university or to recognise the right of the students to appoint the professors.

text: Shanghai, April 1.—The N. C. D. News commenting on the departure of the Mongugai says the departure appears to have been interpreted in some quarters as a political event of first class importance in relation to Russian affairs in the Far East, being said to indicate the end of the White Monarchist group. In point of fact it is nothing of the kind, and simply means that the so-called Cossack General and his band of Cossacks have decided to return to Russia, a very sensible thing to do considering the unfortunate circumstances in which they found themselves here, stranded and virtually existing on charity.—Reuter.

An interminable procession of motor cars crawled up the slopes of the Mount of Olives last night to the Government House where Sir Herbert Samuel's brilliant reception on the eve of Lord Balfour's opening of the new Hebrew University was held.
It was a picturesque and historic assemblage and included Lord Allenby, Mr. Chaim Weizmann and numerous delegates. All Palestine was represented. Ecclesiastics of every sect from Abyssinians, Copts, from sombre black to whiteclad Dominican friars, Lord Balfour was the most noteworthy figure present, overtopping the rest and looking very fit and very cheerful.

label: text

The University was built on Mount Scopus and designed to be the centre of advanced research in all branches of science and learning, for which Palestine offers special facilities. It includes a microbiological institute to investigate local infectious diseases, which will form the nucleus of medical faculty. Another institute will form the nucleus of a chemical faculty. Still another will specialise in Jewish religion literature, law and language. Teaching will be provided for Arabs.
